title: How to start 3D design from scratch: pattern making and creating a top in CLO?

chunks.title: How to start 3D design from scratch: pattern making and creating a top in CLO?
chunks.content: # How to Start 3D Design from Scratch: Pattern Making and Creating a Top in CLO This document provides a detailed guide on using CLO software for 2D pattern making and creating a top garment, covering size settings, fabric selection, pattern drafting, adjustments, sewing, and simulation. --- ## Setting Up the Virtual Model and Size Table in CLO This section explains how to configure the virtual avatar, set measurement units, and apply a US standard size table (ASTM Missy Size 10) for accurate pattern drafting. - The size table used is the US standard ASTM Missy Size 10, with units in inches. - To set units to inches, go to User Self-Definition Settings and change units; a software restart is required. - In the 2D window (plating window), select the avatar "Feifei" as the virtual model. - In the SIZE information box, select **US ASTM Missy Curvy** size 10 to update the avatar’s measurements. --- ## Fabric Selection and 2D Interface Setup This section covers fabric selection and preparing the workspace for symmetrical pattern creation. - Search for and select the fabric "muslin 22x22" in the fabric library. - Switch the 2D interface to full 2D display to work with left-right symmetrical top and bottom panels. - The pattern size table is set relative to the right-hand side blue grid, approximately one-third scale. --- ## Drafting the Basic Top Pattern This section details how to draft the top pattern including chest width, back length, and key dimension marking using CLO's tools. - Create a rectangle representing the widest and longest parts: chest width 9 inches, back middle length 17 inches. - Mark internal lines for key widths and lengths: - Back width: 6.625 inches - Front middle width: 6.25 inches - Middle width: 8.875 inches - Waist width: 6.875 inches - Use the multilinear line tool (shortcut **G**) to draw the outer outline from back length to shoulder height, sleeve length, and bottom line. - Draw front outline focusing on collar and sleeve length; the rest mirrors the back. - Convert back and front outlines into multilinear lines (shortcut **C**), and smooth curves using the curve tool (shortcut **V**). - Adjust sleeve outline slope with the multilinear tool. --- ## Refining Pattern Pieces and Adjusting Points This section guides on selecting pattern pieces, flipping, cleaning up points, and refining shape lines. - Select outlines and right-click to define back and front pieces. - Flip the front piece horizontally for symmetry. - Use the edit tool to delete extra points and lines, retaining only necessary widths. - Move the side hole 0.375 inches backward to prevent forward shifting. - Adjust back width center by moving 1.8 inches and bottom left by 1.4 inches to align pattern. - Add points on side and middle lines for proper movement and alignment. - Use multilinear tool to smooth stiff center lines. - Move the shoulder line forward by 0.5 inches in the size table.
chunks.content_description:
I want to create a garment in CLO starting from making the pattern pieces. Is that possible?  
Of course it is!!!

chunks.content: - Use the edit tool to delete extra points and lines, retaining only necessary widths. - Move the side hole 0.375 inches backward to prevent forward shifting. - Adjust back width center by moving 1.8 inches and bottom left by 1.4 inches to align pattern. - Add points on side and middle lines for proper movement and alignment. - Use multilinear tool to smooth stiff center lines. - Move the shoulder line forward by 0.5 inches in the size table. - Cut and merge shoulder lines between front and back for a continuous seam. - Convert sharp points on shoulder lines to curve points to avoid interference. --- ## Creating and Adjusting Line Paths and Seams This section focuses on creating seam paths, adding cut points, and ensuring smooth, straight seams. - Use the plus point division tool (shortcut **X**) to add cut points on the outer board line, 2 inches from the shoulder line. - Use the editor board tool (shortcut **Z**) to add lines with specific width (1.2 inches) and joint length (4.5 inches) for sewing seam allowance. - Align curve points to straighten side seams. - Extend side seams by 1 inch on shoulder line points to ensure front and back side seams are parallel and equal in length. - Add the waist line 3 inches from the front center; depth is 0.5 inches (half). - Use plus point division tool to add a 3.5-inch section for the waistline. - Adjust waist width to match size table (target 13.75 inches vs. current 11.954 inches) by moving front and back points outward by approximately 0.898 inches each. - Add and adjust shoulder lines using average segment and edit sheet tools, with final adjustments made for smoothness and symmetry. --- ## Finalizing Shoulder Line and Panel Arrangements This section describes shoulder line augmentation, panel merging, and layout preparation for sewing. - Remove 0.5 inches from the back shoulder line to finalize. - Use edit sheet tool and Ctrl+click to insert extension points near the sleeve ball. - Extend points by 0.5 inches to complete shoulder adjustments. - Select front and back panels, right-click and merge symmetrical panels using Ctrl+D and Shift for horizontal layout. - Adjust merging points for better panel alignment. - Arrange panels on the virtual model using arrangement points (shortcut Shift+F). --- ## Sewing and Simulation Setup This section explains how to apply automatic sewing, check sewing lines, and run garment simulation. - Use the automatic sewing tool: - Set clothing type to "top" - Advanced type set to 5 - Confirm system sewing lines and run the simulation. - Use the circular measurement tool in the 3D window to measure shoulder line and dress line lengths. - Attach dress lines to the model and verify garment balance. - Adjust fabric visualization to translucent to observe seam allowance. - Reduce seam allowance to 0.5 inches; adjust unequal seam sides simultaneously using right-click "adjust seam" option. - Final seam allowance is approximately 0.757 inches after adjustments.

Final seam allowance is approximately 0.757 inches after adjustments. - Modify bottom side seam points by dragging 0.25 inches to avoid sharp corners. --- ## Checking Seam Adhesion and Adjusting Sewing Lines This section outlines how to verify smooth seam connections and adjust sewing lines for proper fit. - Use the copy function to duplicate front and back pieces and check seam circle smoothness. - Adjust individual curve points using the edit curve point tool to ensure 90-degree angles at seams. - Extend seams if adhesion points differ due to short seam length. - Adjust pre-central shapes and free-line points for natural transitions and smooth angles near 90 degrees. - Use shortcut **V** to toggle visibility and adjust free-line points and pre-central shape lengths. --- ## Adding Cutouts and Final Adjustments on the Top Pattern This section details how to add cutouts on shoulder and side seams with precise measurements. - Measure shoulder length on the back piece. - Use the cutout tool in the 2D toolbar to add cutouts on shoulder lines of front and back pieces. - Adjust shoulder line lengths to match exactly (e.g., front piece length 2.311 inches, back piece 2.305 inches). - Add cutouts on side seams with matching lengths for front and back pieces. --- ## Creating and Adjusting Sleeve Pattern This section covers drafting the sleeve pattern, marking dimensions, and applying curve adjustments. - Create a sleeve curve with widest width 6.25 inches and length 22 inches. - Mark 6-inch height on the sleeve using internal line tools. - Use plus point line tool to mark sleeve width at 4 inches. - Use internal multiline tool to draft sleeve outline. - Divide sleeve into 3 parts and move equal division points 0.5 inches toward 45° angle. - Adjust sleeve curve using decimal dot and version tools to control wireless degree. - Align sleeve seam lines and adjust curve handles for smoothness. - Confirm sleeve measurements; minor differences do not require changes. - Remove linkage of sleeve version and move points individually. - Use comparison version length tool to add cutouts on sleeve edges. - Convert inner sleeve lines to baseline for effective cutout application. - Adjust shoulder line positions using the edit version tool. - Add two-sided plate cutouts on sleeve and shoulder line junctions. - Use automatic sewing tool to arrange sewing lines and simulate sleeve.

markdown_content: # How to Start 3D Design from Scratch: Pattern Making and Creating a Top in CLO This document provides a detailed guide on using CLO software for 2D pattern making and creating a top garment, covering size settings, fabric selection, pattern drafting, adjustments, sewing, and simulation. --- ## Setting Up the Virtual Model and Size Table in CLO This section explains how to configure the virtual avatar, set measurement units, and apply a US standard size table (ASTM Missy Size 10) for accurate pattern drafting. - The size table used is the US standard ASTM Missy Size 10, with units in inches. - To set units to inches, go to User Self-Definition Settings and change units; a software restart is required. - In the 2D window (plating window), select the avatar "Feifei" as the virtual model. - In the SIZE information box, select **US ASTM Missy Curvy** size 10 to update the avatar’s measurements. --- ## Fabric Selection and 2D Interface Setup This section covers fabric selection and preparing the workspace for symmetrical pattern creation. - Search for and select the fabric "muslin 22x22" in the fabric library. - Switch the 2D interface to full 2D display to work with left-right symmetrical top and bottom panels. - The pattern size table is set relative to the right-hand side blue grid, approximately one-third scale. --- ## Drafting the Basic Top Pattern This section details how to draft the top pattern including chest width, back length, and key dimension marking using CLO's tools. - Create a rectangle representing the widest and longest parts: chest width 9 inches, back middle length 17 inches. - Mark internal lines for key widths and lengths: - Back width: 6.625 inches - Front middle width: 6.25 inches - Middle width: 8.875 inches - Waist width: 6.875 inches - Use the multilinear line tool (shortcut **G**) to draw the outer outline from back length to shoulder height, sleeve length, and bottom line. - Draw front outline focusing on collar and sleeve length; the rest mirrors the back. - Convert back and front outlines into multilinear lines (shortcut **C**), and smooth curves using the curve tool (shortcut **V**). - Adjust sleeve outline slope with the multilinear tool. --- ## Refining Pattern Pieces and Adjusting Points This section guides on selecting pattern pieces, flipping, cleaning up points, and refining shape lines. - Select outlines and right-click to define back and front pieces. - Flip the front piece horizontally for symmetry. - Use the edit tool to delete extra points and lines, retaining only necessary widths. - Move the side hole 0.375 inches backward to prevent forward shifting. - Adjust back width center by moving 1.8 inches and bottom left by 1.4 inches to align pattern. - Add points on side and middle lines for proper movement and alignment. - Use multilinear tool to smooth stiff center lines. - Move the shoulder line forward by 0.5 inches in the size table. - Cut and merge shoulder lines between front and back for a continuous seam. - Convert sharp points on shoulder lines to curve points to avoid interference. --- ## Creating and Adjusting Line Paths and Seams This section focuses on creating seam paths, adding cut points, and ensuring smooth, straight seams. - Use the plus point division tool (shortcut **X**) to add cut points on the outer board line, 2 inches from the shoulder line. - Use the editor board tool (shortcut **Z**) to add lines with specific width (1.2 inches) and joint length (4.5 inches) for sewing seam allowance. - Align curve points to straighten side seams. - Extend side seams by 1 inch on shoulder line points to ensure front and back side seams are parallel and equal in length. - Add the waist line 3 inches from the front center; depth is 0.5 inches (half). - Use plus point division tool to add a 3.5-inch section for the waistline. - Adjust waist width to match size table (target 13.75 inches vs. current 11.954 inches) by moving front and back points outward by approximately 0.898 inches each. - Add and adjust shoulder lines using average segment and edit sheet tools, with final adjustments made for smoothness and symmetry. --- ## Finalizing Shoulder Line and Panel Arrangements This section describes shoulder line augmentation, panel merging, and layout preparation for sewing. - Remove 0.5 inches from the back shoulder line to finalize. - Use edit sheet tool and Ctrl+click to insert extension points near the sleeve ball. - Extend points by 0.5 inches to complete shoulder adjustments. - Select front and back panels, right-click and merge symmetrical panels using Ctrl+D and Shift for horizontal layout. - Adjust merging points for better panel alignment. - Arrange panels on the virtual model using arrangement points (shortcut Shift+F). --- ## Sewing and Simulation Setup This section explains how to apply automatic sewing, check sewing lines, and run garment simulation. - Use the automatic sewing tool: - Set clothing type to "top" - Advanced type set to 5 - Confirm system sewing lines and run the simulation. - Use the circular measurement tool in the 3D window to measure shoulder line and dress line lengths. - Attach dress lines to the model and verify garment balance. - Adjust fabric visualization to translucent to observe seam allowance. - Reduce seam allowance to 0.5 inches; adjust unequal seam sides simultaneously using right-click "adjust seam" option. - Final seam allowance is approximately 0.757 inches after adjustments. - Modify bottom side seam points by dragging 0.25 inches to avoid sharp corners. --- ## Checking Seam Adhesion and Adjusting Sewing Lines This section outlines how to verify smooth seam connections and adjust sewing lines for proper fit. - Use the copy function to duplicate front and back pieces and check seam circle smoothness. - Adjust individual curve points using the edit curve point tool to ensure 90-degree angles at seams. - Extend seams if adhesion points differ due to short seam length. - Adjust pre-central shapes and free-line points for natural transitions and smooth angles near 90 degrees. - Use shortcut **V** to toggle visibility and adjust free-line points and pre-central shape lengths. --- ## Adding Cutouts and Final Adjustments on the Top Pattern This section details how to add cutouts on shoulder and side seams with precise measurements. - Measure shoulder length on the back piece. - Use the cutout tool in the 2D toolbar to add cutouts on shoulder lines of front and back pieces. - Adjust shoulder line lengths to match exactly (e.g., front piece length 2.311 inches, back piece 2.305 inches). - Add cutouts on side seams with matching lengths for front and back pieces. --- ## Creating and Adjusting Sleeve Pattern This section covers drafting the sleeve pattern, marking dimensions, and applying curve adjustments. - Create a sleeve curve with widest width 6.25 inches and length 22 inches. - Mark 6-inch height on the sleeve using internal line tools. - Use plus point line tool to mark sleeve width at 4 inches. - Use internal multiline tool to draft sleeve outline. - Divide sleeve into 3 parts and move equal division points 0.5 inches toward 45° angle. - Adjust sleeve curve using decimal dot and version tools to control wireless degree. - Align sleeve seam lines and adjust curve handles for smoothness. - Confirm sleeve measurements; minor differences do not require changes. - Remove linkage of sleeve version and move points individually. - Use comparison version length tool to add cutouts on sleeve edges. - Convert inner sleeve lines to baseline for effective cutout application. - Adjust shoulder line positions using the edit version tool. - Add two-sided plate cutouts on sleeve and shoulder line junctions. - Use automatic sewing tool to arrange sewing lines and simulate sleeve. --- ## Posing Virtual Model and Final Simulation Enhancements This section describes adjusting the virtual model’s pose to fit the garment and preparing for final simulation. - Use pose file clip to set model with both hands down. - Enable X-Ray mode to prevent collision between model and garment. - Adjust joint positions manually using positional balls; select the small virtual model icon for simultaneous pose adjustments. - Turn off X-Ray mode with shortcut Shift+X after adjustment. - Remove measurement tape lines on the model by selecting and deleting them in the Edit Measure tool. - Increase garment quality settings before final simulation to improve visual results. - The basic commercial model is now completed and ready for further size table adjustments or combination modeling. --- # Summary This guide thoroughly covers the process of creating a 3D top garment in CLO from scratch using 2D pattern making tools, precise measurements, fabric selection, and detailed adjustments to lines, seams, and panels. It includes instructions on setting up the virtual model, drafting and refining patterns, applying cutouts, sewing line arrangement, sleeve creation, and final simulation setup. The detailed workflow supports efficient and accurate 3D garment design with professional sewing and fitting considerations.
